# Recovery Assertion

## H1 — Goal

Create `util.mjs` exporting `stableSlug(s)`, which lowercases ASCII letters, trims whitespace, replaces runs of non-alphanumeric characters with `-`, and removes leading/trailing `-`. The overall goal also requires `tests.mjs` with at least three `node:assert` cases, including the empty string.

## H2 — Handoff Revision

The governed handoff is `handoff.md` at revision `c2500f027b2e1923b60d99ab3619171e6cf4d69c36109657f4dd60fc7b5a3613`, based on commit `ec7eb3635274085b54fa2f62046669f35252eea7`.

## H3 — Verified State

No work is verified. The ledger contains no bound verification receipt from a Conductor distinct from the executor.

## H4 — Unverified / In-Progress State

Round `R-01`, slice `S1`, is prepared but has recorded no executor actions. Direct observation of the slice target `util.mjs` returned no content. That observation is not verified progress; its worktree or commit status is unverified, and any uncommitted state must be treated only as observation.

## H5 — Pending Action

Implement only slice `S1`: make `util.mjs` export `stableSlug` with the required lowercase, trim, non-alphanumeric run replacement, and leading/trailing dash removal behavior, so it can be accepted by direct inspection.

## H6 — Blockers

No substantive blocker is recorded. No deterministic checks are declared for this slice. Verification and completion remain unavailable to the executor because they require the governed Gate, independent review, and a Conductor-authored bound receipt.

## H7 — Legal Next Action

The next legal action is a single in-scope edit to `util.mjs` implementing the `S1` contract. Work must stop if scope drift occurs.

## H8 — Non-Goals / Forbidden Scope

No scope beyond the stated task is authorized. Do not touch `.tad/scripts/`, `.claude/`, or `.tad/hooks/`. Do not inspect hidden acceptance, start another slice, redo verified work, or declare completion. Strict Phase 2 also denies Shell/Bash and agent spawning; only Conductor-side predeclared deterministic checks may run.

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal

Editing `util.mjs` is legal because `S1` expressly targets that file, its required outcome is the `stableSlug` implementation, and `util.mjs` is listed among the slice’s allowed paths.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone

The packet explicitly forbids redoing verified work because verification is authoritative ledger state. There is currently no verified work to redo; if verification later advances, that work must be preserved rather than repeated.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry / Self-Completion Is Unavailable

There is no recorded failed attempt authorizing a retry, and uncommitted observations cannot establish progress or failure. The executor cannot self-verify or self-complete: checkpoints, ordinary files, completion prose, and self-authored receipts do not advance `verified`.

## S4 — Rejected Actions

Rejected actions include implementing `tests.mjs` or any later slice during `S1`; treating the empty observed target as completed or verified; blindly retrying unknown prior work; declaring success; running undeclared checks; inspecting hidden acceptance; spawning agents; using Shell/Bash for execution; changing files outside the allowed paths; and touching any forbidden-scope directory.
